facts.text: The brown honeyeater is the only honeyeater found west of the Wallace Line, occurring on the island of Bali.
facts.quote: the brown honeyeater is unique in that it also occurs on the island of Bali, making it the only honeyeater to be found west of the Wallace Line

facts.text: This plain grey-brown bird hides a small yellow patch behind the eye and dull yellow-olive panels in its folded wings and tail.
facts.quote: The only distinguishing features are a small yellow patch behind the eye, which is indistinct in some birds, and dull yellow-olive panels in the folded wings and tail.

facts.text: Its slender, slightly curved black bill is well adapted for probing deep into tubular flowers.
facts.quote: The bill is black, and is long, slender, and curved slightly downwards, well adapted for probing deep tubular flowers.

facts.text: Both sexes call, usually early in the morning, though the male keeps calling throughout the day during the breeding season.
facts.quote: Both sexes call, usually early in the morning, though the male calls throughout the day during the breeding season.

facts.text: This busy acrobat hovers over flowers and chases insects in flight, feeding mainly in the canopy but sometimes on the ground.
facts.quote: A busy, acrobatic bird, the brown honeyeater is frequently on the wing, hovering over flowers and pursuing insects in flight.

facts.text: Both parents build the woven cup nest of grass and soft bark, with the male standing guard while the female builds.
facts.quote: Both sexes contribute to the nest building, though the male also stands guard while the female is building the nest.

facts.text: Numbers are rising in urban parks and gardens, but this brings new dangers from cats, cars and window collisions.
facts.quote: Numbers are increasing in urban areas, particularly in parks and gardens and around farms; however, the new habitats have increased the incidences of death from cats, cars and collisions with windows.

facts.text: Its loud, clear, musical song has been described as the best of all the honeyeaters.
facts.quote: It has a loud, clear, musical song, described as the best of all the honeyeaters.

facts.text: It is seasonally nomadic, following flowering food plants within its local area.
facts.quote: The brown honeyeater is seasonally nomadic across its local area in response to flowering food plants.

facts.text: Its call sweet-sweet-quarty-quarty is very loud for the size of the bird.
facts.quote: It has a clear, rolling, musical call, rendered as sweet-sweet-quarty-quarty, which is very loud for the size of the bird.
